implementation_notes: Thread::Queue is the in-process channel and Ruby 3.2 added the timed pull: pop(timeout: sec) returns nil when the interval expires, which is the receive-with-timeout half of the pattern, pop(non_block: true) is the receiveNoWait, and SizedQueue bounds the channel so producers block instead of the consumer falling behind. Message libraries repeat the shape at the transport boundary (a pop that returns nil on an empty queue, a blocking subscribe where push is available), so a hand-written loop is only needed on older Rubies or for channels without a timeout argument.
code_sketch:
loop do
  msg = q.pop(timeout: idle)   # nil = idle tick (Ruby 3.2+)
  if msg.nil?
    backoff                    # explicit idle policy, no hot spin
  else
    handle(msg)                # ack: the message left the queue
  end
end
pitfalls: A bare pop with no timeout blocks forever, so a shutdown flag is never observed and the thread only wakes on a message or on Thread#kill; the timed form is what makes graceful stop possible.
pop(timeout:) and the non_block argument are mutually exclusive and raise ArgumentError when combined, which is the porting trap for pre-3.2 code that polled with non_block plus sleep.
The GVL means CPU-bound batch handling starves other Ruby threads; only blocking I/O releases it, so heavy processing belongs off the polling thread.
